sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是99%隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Ruman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Britt Young is a geographer and tech writer based in the Bay Area, and she loves a good theme party.
sentences.zh: 布里特·杨是一位住在湾区的地理学家兼科技作家，她热衷于办各种主题派对。

sentences.en: My whole life I've done some silly themed parties.
sentences.zh: 我这一辈子办过不少有趣的搞怪主题派对。

sentences.en: And when she says silly, she's not exaggerating.
sentences.zh: 当她说有趣时，她可一点也没夸张。

sentences.en: Producer Vivian Lay.
sentences.zh: 制作人薇薇安·雷。

sentences.en: She told me about a party she threw once based on an obscure sitcom about a rural Canadian farming community.
sentences.zh: 她跟我讲过她曾经办过的一个派对，灵感来自一部关于加拿大农村农耕社区的冷门情景喜剧。

sentences.en: She also used to host annual ragers in honor of Billy Mays.
sentences.zh: 她以前还经常为了纪念比利·梅斯而举办一年一度的狂欢派对。

sentences.en: You know, that guy from the OxyClean infomercials.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就是演氧净电视购物广告的那个人。

sentences.en: Roman Mars here for 99PI.
sentences.zh: 这里是罗曼·马尔斯，为您带来99PI节目。

sentences.en: But a few years ago, she threw her wildest party yet.
sentences.zh: 但几年前，她举办了迄今为止最疯狂的一次派对。

sentences.en: It was an arm party.
sentences.zh: 那是一个“手臂派对”。

sentences.en: Britt has what's called a congenital upper limb deficiency.
sentences.zh: 布里特患有先天性上肢缺失症。

sentences.en: In other words, she was born without the part of her arm just below her left elbow.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，她出生时左肘下方的手臂就缺失了。

sentences.en: This latest celebration was a farewell to her boring old prosthesis and a welcome home to her brand new
sentences.zh: 这场最新的庆祝活动既是对她那无聊旧假肢的告别，也是对她全新...

sentences.en: multi-articulating bionic hand.
sentences.zh: 多关节仿生手的欢迎仪式。

sentences.en: We had a friend who played bartender, and we had a bunch of arm-themed cocktails.
sentences.zh: 我们请了一位朋友来当调酒师，还准备了一堆以手臂为主题的鸡尾酒。

sentences.en: There was Armageddon, Pink Armadillo, a bunch of things like that.
sentences.zh: 有“末日手臂”、“粉红犰狳”，诸如此类的一大堆。

sentences.en: There were also arm-themed games like Arm Twister.
sentences.zh: 现场还有手臂主题的游戏，比如“手臂扭扭乐”。

sentences.en: Which was normal Twister, but anytime that you needed assistance, you could grab a free prosthetic arm to reach Yellow 5 easier or whatever.
sentences.zh: 其实就是普通的扭扭乐，但每当你需要帮助时，你都可以抓起一只免费的假肢，以便更容易地够到黄色5号格之类的。

sentences.en: She even christened the high-tech arm by cutting a cake with it.
sentences.zh: 她甚至用这只高科技手臂切蛋糕来为它举行落成仪式。

sentences.en: I'm really trying to be Twitter famous, so please tweet it.
sentences.zh: 我真的很想在推特上火一把，所以请大家发条推文吧。

sentences.en: And this is not going to work.
sentences.zh: 而且这招行不通。

sentences.en: Here we go, yay!
sentences.zh: 来吧，耶！

sentences.en: It just opened.
sentences.zh: 它刚打开。

sentences.en: Um, so that's the, that's the, uh, what's that called?
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以那个，那个，呃，那个叫什么来着？

sentences.en: It's a fiSt.
sentences.zh: 这是一个拳头。

sentences.en: This is the sound of Britt giving me a little demo of how her prosthetic hand works over Zoom.
sentences.zh: 这是布里特通过Zoom向我演示她的仿生手如何工作时的声音。

sentences.en: We ended up playing sort of a game of cyborg charades while she cycled through the different grip modes of her prosthesis.
sentences.zh: 我们最后玩了一场类似赛博格猜词的游戏，同时她切换着假肢不同的抓握模式。

sentences.en: I call this one the Obama talking point.
sentences.zh: 我把这个叫作奥巴马的论点。

sentences.en: It's the thumb resting on top of the index finger, and you're like, so you go, yes.
sentences.zh: 就是大拇指搭在食指上面，然后你就说，所以你会说，对。

sentences.en: This one might be like, I am a sophisticated cyborg, and I am handing you my credit card.
sentences.zh: 这个可能就像是，我是一个成熟的赛博格，现在我要把信用卡递给你。

sentences.en: And so this one is like, Italian?
sentences.zh: 然后这个就像是，意大利人？

sentences.en: This prosthetic hand has a sleek carbon fiber casing with specific pre-programmed grips that she can control just by flexing the muscles in her residual limb.
sentences.zh: 这款仿生手拥有时尚的碳纤维外壳，带有特定的预设抓握模式，她只需收缩残端肌肉就能进行控制。

sentences.en: She can use a precision pinch to pick a hairpin up off the table, or a Hulk-style power fist to squeeze objects.
sentences.zh: 她可以用精细捏取从桌上捡起一根发夹，或者像绿巨人一样用强力拳头挤压物体。

sentences.en: This kind of assistive technology has been life-changing for a lot of people who have limb differences.
sentences.zh: 这种辅助技术改变了许多肢体残障人士的生活。

sentences.en: But for Britt in particular, it hasn't been life-changing at all.
sentences.zh: 但对布里特本人来说，它根本没有改变她的生活。

sentences.en: In fact, her cutting-edge bionic arm has been a pretty major disappointment.
sentences.zh: 事实上，她这只尖端的仿生手臂可以说是相当大的一个失望。

sentences.en: It's just not, it's not what you imagine.
sentences.zh: 它根本不是，不是你想象的那样。

sentences.en: It's not like, well, I'm like everyone else now.
sentences.zh: 它不是那种，嗯，我现在和大家一样了。

sentences.en: It's something different.
sentences.zh: 它是某种不同的东西。

sentences.en: It's something different.
sentences.zh: 它是某种不同的东西。

sentences.en: Prosthetics go back thousands of years.
sentences.zh: 假肢的历史可以追溯到几千年前。

sentences.en: The earliest known prosthesis is actually a wooden toe that dates back to ancient Egypt.
sentences.zh: 目前已知最早的假肢其实是一根可以追溯到古埃及的木脚趾。

sentences.en: But while we've had prosthetics forever, we've only seen major advancements in their design in the last couple hundred years, mostly thanks to the military.
sentences.zh: 然而，尽管我们拥有假肢的历史极为悠久，但其设计的大幅跃进却只发生在过去两百年间，这主要归功于军队。

sentences.en: Their development is intricately, intimately, inextricably tied to the military.
sentences.zh: 它们的发展与军队复杂、密切且不可分割地联系在一起。

sentences.en: This is David Serlin, Associate Professor of Communication and Science Studies at UC San Diego.
sentences.zh: 这位是加州大学圣迭戈分校传播与科学研究副教授大卫·塞尔林。

sentences.en: He says that the first major leap in prosthetics came after the Civil War, which was considered the first modern war.
sentences.zh: 他说，假肢领域的第一次重大飞跃出现在南北战争之后，这场战争被认为是第一场现代战争。

sentences.en: The scale of damage from weapons was unprecedented.
sentences.zh: 武器造成的破坏规模是前所未有的。

sentences.en: And so people hadn't really seen what prosthetics could do on kind of the scale that they would soon come to understand.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们此前并未真正见识过假肢在他们即将见证的这种规模下能发挥什么作用。

sentences.en: By the end of the war, tens of thousands of soldiers suffered amputations and needed help getting back to their lives.
sentences.zh: 到战争结束时，成千上万的士兵遭受了截肢，需要帮助来恢复生活。

sentences.en: In response, the federal government began subsidizing artificial limbs for Union soldiers, and prosthetic companies sprang up to meet the spike in demand.
sentences.zh: 作为回应，联邦政府开始为北军士兵的人工假肢提供补贴，假肢公司也如雨后春笋般涌现，以满足飙升的需求。

sentences.en: In the process, available prosthetic technology for both veterans and civilians grew exponentially.
sentences.zh: 在这个过程中，退伍军人和平民可用的假肢技术都呈指数级增长。

sentences.en: Prostheses evolved from rudimentary wooden peg legs to artificial limbs that had hinges at the ankles and knees to reproduce a natural gait.
sentences.zh: 假肢从最初简陋的木质假腿，演变成在脚踝和膝盖处设有铰链、能重现自然步态的人工假肢。

sentences.en: Then, decades later, World War II led to even more prosthetic innovation.
sentences.zh: 几十年后，第二次世界大战带来了更多的假肢创新。

sentences.en: Engineering science, material science, those are all percolating in the 30s and 40s, and they really take off during and after World War II.
sentences.zh: 工程科学、材料科学，这些都在30和40年代酝酿，并在二战期间及其后真正腾飞。

sentences.en: In the Soviet Union, in the U.S., in Britain, the development of what we think of as prosthetic science, they really become industries.
sentences.zh: 在苏联、美国、英国，我们今天所理解的假肢科学的发展，真正变成了各大产业。

sentences.en: In the United States, a team of military personnel, engineers,
sentences.zh: 在美国，由军事人员、工程师组成的团队

sentences.en: and prosthetists came together at the request of the Surgeon General of the Army to form the Committee on Prosthetics Research and Development.
sentences.zh: 和假肢矫形师应陆军军医总长之邀齐聚一堂，成立了假肢研究与发展委员会。

sentences.en: They wanted to figure out how to actually develop prosthetics into a proper field of medicine.
sentences.zh: 他们想弄清楚如何将假肢真正发展成为一个成熟的医学领域。

sentences.en: And the biggest challenge was developing a good artificial hand.
sentences.zh: 而最大的挑战在于开发出一只优秀的人工手。

sentences.en: Prosthetic legs are simpler to design, and users tend to have higher satisfaction rates with them.
sentences.zh: 假肢腿的设计更简单，使用者对它们的满意度也往往更高。

sentences.en: But creating a hand that incorporated robotics wasn't possible until well into the Cold War.
sentences.zh: 但要制造出一只融入机器人技术的手，直到冷战时期才真正成为可能。

sentences.en: The 60s and 70s, there are all of these engineering sciences that develop between, let's say, the military and like MIT or Northwestern.
sentences.zh: 在60和70年代，所有这些工程科学都在比方说军方与麻省理工学院或西北大学之间发展起来。

sentences.en: So instead of just developing napalm, they're also developing technologies that allow you to use batteries for what are called myoelectric arMs.
sentences.zh: 所以他们不仅在研制凝固汽油弹，还在研发让你能用电池驱动所谓肌电手臂的技术。

sentences.en: A myoelectric arm is a battery-powered prosthesis that can be controlled by movements on the residual limb.
sentences.zh: 肌电手臂是一种电池供电的假肢，可以通过残端动作来进行控制。

sentences.en: In the early 1990s, Britt actually became one of the youngest children in the country to get one.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪90年代初，布里特其实成为了国内获得这种假肢的年龄最小的儿童之一。

sentences.en: I wasn't the first, but I was part of one of the earliest cohorts of babies, basically, using myoelectric hands.
sentences.zh: 我不是第一个，但基本上属于最早使用肌电手的那批婴儿群体之一。

sentences.en: At the time, these myoelectric hands were state-of-the-art compared to anything else on the market.
sentences.zh: 在当时，与市场上任何其他产品相比，这些肌电手堪称最先进的技术。

sentences.en: But all that Britt's hand could really do was pinch open and shut.
sentences.zh: 但布里特的手真正能做的事情仅仅是开合捏握。

sentences.en: She worked with these devices all the way through middle school.
sentences.zh: 她一直带着这些设备上完了初中。

sentences.en: And it was a real crowd-pleaser in the seventh grade.
sentences.zh: 这在七年级时特别讨人喜欢。

sentences.en: It was like a party trick in middle school.
sentences.zh: 它就像是初中里的一个小把戏。

sentences.en: We were like, hey, I can crush a can.
sentences.zh: 我们当时会说，嘿，我能捏碎一个罐子。

sentences.en: And, you know, that's fun for a while.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这好玩了一阵子。

sentences.en: But as Britt got older, she realized just how useless her myoelectric hand really was.
sentences.zh: 但随着布里特渐渐长大，她意识到自己的肌电手其实是多么的无用。

sentences.en: If you think about it, how many tasks in your day do you need a slow-moving, grinding-clicking thing
sentences.zh: 如果你仔细想想，你一天中有多少任务需要这样一个动作缓慢、发出咯吱咯吱声、

sentences.en: that will grip in a single motion, more like a pinch?
sentences.zh: 只能以单一动作抓握（更像是捏取）的东西？

sentences.en: It couldn't even grab a piece of paper.
sentences.zh: 它甚至抓不起一张纸。

sentences.en: It would just slide right through.
sentences.zh: 纸会直接从中间滑过去。

sentences.en: And by the time she got into high school, she was pretty over it.
sentences.zh: 等她上了高中，她就对这东西相当厌烦了。

sentences.en: This thing doesn't help me.
sentences.zh: 这东西对我一点帮助也没有。

sentences.en: It's heavy.
sentences.zh: 它很重。

sentences.en: And I'm just going to quit.
sentences.zh: 我打算不干了。

sentences.en: So I went exclusively to passive arms after that.
sentences.zh: 所以在那之后我完全改用被动式手臂了。

sentences.en: A passive prosthesis, also called a cosmetic prosthesis, is a device that closely resembles a quote-unquote natural limb.
sentences.zh: 被动式假肢，也称为外观假肢，是一种外观极度类似于所谓“自然肢体”的设备。

sentences.en: It doesn't crush any cans or get you any attention.
sentences.zh: 它捏不碎任何罐子，也不会为你赢得任何关注。

sentences.en: In fact, it serves the opposite purpose.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它的作用恰恰相反。

sentences.en: To help you blend in.
sentences.zh: 是为了帮你融入人群。

sentences.en: Something that I had deeply ingrained in me over my lifetime, that, like, I needed to wear this or else people are going to treat me differently.
sentences.zh: 这是我一生中根深蒂固的想法，也就是我必须戴着这个，否则人们会用异样的眼光看我。

sentences.en: They're going to look at me funny.
sentences.zh: 他们会奇怪地看着我。

sentences.en: I need to wear this so that I am undetected and that I can conform and that my life runs smoother.
sentences.zh: 我必须戴着它，这样我就不会被察觉，可以与常人合群，生活才能过得更顺畅。

sentences.en: After her bad experience with the myoelectric arm, she had no interest in dabbling in advanced prosthetics anymore.
sentences.zh: 在经历了肌电手臂带来的糟糕体验后，她再也没有兴趣涉足先进的假肢技术了。

sentences.en: She was resigned to just staying undetected.
sentences.zh: 她甘愿就这样保持不被察觉。

sentences.en: That is, until a few years ago, when her prosthetist reached out.
sentences.zh: 直到几年前，她的假肢矫形师联系了她。

sentences.en: They got in touch with me and they said, you know, there's been a lot of changes in prosthetic arm technology.
sentences.zh: 他们联系我说，你知道的，假肢手臂技术已经有了很大的变化。

sentences.en: Things are a lot more sophisticated.
sentences.zh: 现在的技术要先进得多。

sentences.en: In the years since Brits stopped using powered devices, innovation in the field had gone into hyperdrive.
sentences.zh: 自从布里特停止使用动力设备以来，该领域的创新便进入了快车道。

sentences.en: These new advancements in prosthetics were driven in the early 2000s by a renewed sense of government responsibility
sentences.zh: 在2000年代初，假肢技术的这些新进展是由政府新一轮的责任感推动的，

sentences.en: to compensate for the inadequacies of the American healthcare system.
sentences.zh: 即弥补美国医疗体系的不足。

sentences.en: No, I'm just kidding.
sentences.zh: 不，我开玩笑的。

sentences.en: It was because of the military again.
sentences.zh: 还是因为军队的缘故。

sentences.en: The Iraq War was a really big turning point in prosthetics in the U.S., but also in parts of Europe.
sentences.zh: 伊拉克战争是美国以及欧洲部分地区假肢技术的一个重大转折点。

sentences.en: In 2006, DARPA launched the Revolutionizing Prosthetics Program in response to the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 2006年，为了应对伊拉克和阿富汗战争，美国国防部高级研究计划局（DARPA）启动了“革命性假肢项目”。

sentences.en: They wanted to address the shortcomings of available prosthetics for veterans with amputations
sentences.zh: 他们希望通过打造终极动力手来解决现有假肢对截肢退伍军人的局限性，

sentences.en: by building the ultimate powered hand that would be sleeker and multi-articulating,
sentences.zh: 这种手将更加流线型且具有多关节，

sentences.en: meaning the individual digits on the hand could move and form different grip patterns.
sentences.zh: 这意味着手上的各个手指可以移动并形成不同的抓握模式。

sentences.en: And this time around, they wanted these new high-tech prosthetics to look bionic.
sentences.zh: 而这一次，他们希望这些全新的高科技假肢看起来具有仿生感。

sentences.en: The goal 30, 40 years ago in prosthetics was to make things look realistic and to be able to pass.
sentences.zh: 30、40年前假肢的目标是让东西看起来逼真，并且能够乱真。

sentences.en: David Serlin again.
sentences.zh: 又是大卫·塞尔林的话。

sentences.en: But now you do tend to see prosthetics that are the last thing that they're interested in doing is looking like the quote-unquote real thing.
sentences.zh: 但现在你确实往往会看到这样的假肢：它们最不感兴趣的事情就是看起来像所谓的“真品”。

sentences.en: They will have articulated fingers or articulated joints, but they're not looking to mimic the way that the human flesh-colored elbow joint or knee joint or finger joints look.
sentences.zh: 它们会有活动的关节或手指，但它们并不打算模仿人类肉色肘关节、膝关节或指关节的外观。

sentences.en: In fact, what they look more like are robots out of Star Trek or Star Wars.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它们看起来更像是《星际迷航》或《星球大战》里的机器人。

sentences.en: We'd seen articulating bionic limbs in movies and comic books for decades, and now it seemed like real-world prosthetics were finally getting closer to our sci-fi dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 我们在电影和漫画书中看到有节的仿生肢体已经有几十年了，现在看来，现实世界的假肢终于更接近我们的科幻梦想了。

sentences.en: Like, I mean, we've always had sci-fi movies be the standard for what we want in the future, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，科幻电影一直都是我们对未来期望的标准，对吧？

sentences.en: And there's just like this turn in like, okay, what's possible?
sentences.zh: 然后人们的观念发生了转变，开始思考：究竟什么才是可能的？

sentences.en: And there seemed to be kind of like a weird alignment in the early 2000s,
sentences.zh: 在2000年代初似乎出现了一种奇怪的契合，

sentences.en: where what was potentially possible technologically started to line up more with like this vision of what is going to be attainable.
sentences.zh: 当时潜在的技术可能性开始与这种“未来必将实现”的愿景更加一致。

sentences.en: He's got a hell of a grip.
sentences.zh: 他的握力可真强啊。

sentences.en: And that is like perfectly replaceable prosthetic limbs.
sentences.zh: 而这就像是完全可以替代的假肢。

sentences.en: You have a metal arm?
sentences.zh: 你有一条金属手臂？

sentences.en: That is awesome, dude.
sentences.zh: 太酷了，老兄。

sentences.en: So in 2018, tempted by all of these new advances in the technology, Britt decided to get her first myoelectric prosthesis in over 15 years.
sentences.zh: 因此在2018年，经不住所有这些全新技术进步的诱惑，布里特决定配她15年多来的第一款肌电假肢。

sentences.en: There was a lot of anticipation that was being built amongst my friends and myself for what at the time seemed like the coolest, most life-changing,
sentences.zh: 我和朋友们对这款设备充满了期待，在当时它似乎是我一生中将要获得的

sentences.en: cutting-edge prosthetic arm that I would receive in my life.
sentences.zh: 最酷、最具颠覆性、最尖端的假肢手臂。

sentences.en: And I thought it was kind of time to do something really dumb and silly about it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得是时候围绕它做点真正愚蠢又好笑的事情了。

sentences.en: Like throw an arm party.
sentences.zh: 比如办一场手臂派对。

sentences.en: And this is not going to work.
sentences.zh: 而且这招行不通。

sentences.en: Here we go, yeah!
sentences.zh: 来吧，耶！

sentences.en: She was embracing her cyborg future, and it looked awesome.
sentences.zh: 她正在拥抱她的赛博格未来，这看起来酷极了。

sentences.en: People were like, s***.
sentences.zh: 人们都惊呼：靠。

sentences.en: Like when I'm wearing a dress, and I had like a little heel, and then there's this like stormtrooper, like very aggressive-looking, kind of militaristic hand.
sentences.zh: 就像我穿着裙子，踩着小高跟鞋，然后配上这个像冲锋队员一样、看起来极具攻击性、带点军事风格的手臂。

sentences.en: Like, it looked badass.
sentences.zh: 看起来帅呆了。

sentences.en: People love it.
sentences.zh: 人们都很喜欢它。

sentences.en: They just, they want to see tricks.
sentences.zh: 他们就是想看各种把戏。

sentences.en: They want to see like how it moves.
sentences.zh: 他们想看看它是怎么动的。

sentences.en: It was, I mean, like I like the attention.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我喜欢这种关注。

sentences.en: Um, and it's, it felt like middle school again.
sentences.zh: 而且感觉就像回到了初中。

sentences.en: But a lot like when she was in middle school, Britt quickly realized that this high-tech piece of machinery wasn't all that it was hyped up to be.
sentences.zh: 但就像她上初中时一样，布里特很快意识到这个高科技机械并没有被吹捧得那么好。

sentences.en: It was heavy.
sentences.zh: 它很重。

sentences.en: It was hot.
sentences.zh: 它很热。

sentences.en: It was incredibly uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 它让人极其不舒服。

sentences.en: But Britt still practiced with it every day, putting it on and trying to get her body used to the discomfort.
sentences.zh: 但布里特每天仍然坚持练习使用它，把它戴上，努力让自己的身体适应这种不适感。

sentences.en: Maybe it's sort of like breaking in leather heels or something, where you're like, I like the way this looks, and I think I will look sexy.
sentences.zh: 这可能有点像把皮质高跟鞋穿合脚的过程，你会想，我喜欢这个外观，我觉得我这样穿会很性感。

sentences.en: But right now it's pain.
sentences.zh: 但现在只有痛苦。

sentences.en: And you have to endure the pain.
sentences.zh: 你必须忍受这种痛苦。

sentences.en: And the pain wasn't really worth it.
sentences.zh: 而且这种痛苦其实并不值得。

sentences.en: The point of assistive technology like prosthetic devices is to assiSt.
sentences.zh: 像假肢这样的辅助技术的意义在于提供辅助。

sentences.en: But there are a lot of things this multi-articulating hand couldn't do.
sentences.zh: 但这个多关节手有很多事情都做不到。

sentences.en: Simple things, like turning a doorknob.
sentences.zh: 一些简单的事情，比如转动门把手。

sentences.en: So this thing cannot open a doorknob.
sentences.zh: 所以这玩意儿没办法握住门把手。

sentences.en: And turning it.
sentences.zh: 而且旋转它也不行。

sentences.en: Because that's, that's a, that's a forearm rotation.
sentences.zh: 因为那是，那是，那是前臂的旋转。

sentences.en: That's a wrist rotation.
sentences.zh: 那是手腕的旋转。

sentences.en: That's not going to happen.
sentences.zh: 根本做不到。

sentences.en: And it wasn't like she could just make the hand do whatever she wanted.
sentences.zh: 而且也不是说她想让手做什么就能做什么。

sentences.en: She was limited to only the grips that were pre-programmed on the device.
sentences.zh: 她只能使用设备预设好的几种抓握方式。

sentences.en: If you want to do like a thumbs up and then go straight to like a hang 10, how, how?
sentences.zh: 如果你想比个大拇指然后紧接着来个六分仪手势，怎么，怎么弄？

sentences.en: No, no.
sentences.zh: 不行，不行。

sentences.en: So it is multi-articulating.
sentences.zh: 所以它是多关节联动的。

sentences.en: But it is not individually articulating.
sentences.zh: 但它不是单个手指独立运动的。

sentences.en: Like, there are presets.
sentences.zh: 类似于，它有预设模式。

sentences.en: And that's it.
sentences.zh: 就这样。

sentences.en: I can't, like, decide to use the middle finger.
sentences.zh: 我不能随心所欲地决定去用中指。

sentences.en: Oh, that's not even an option?
sentences.zh: 哦，那甚至都不是个选项？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: And also it's proprietary.
sentences.zh: 而且它还是专有技术的。

sentences.en: So if you would like to change the grip patterns, you must make an appointment with
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想更改抓握模式，你必须预约

sentences.en: your prosthetiSt.
sentences.zh: 你的假肢师。

sentences.en: There were actually only a few tasks that her bionic hand was helpful for.
sentences.zh: 事实上，她的仿生手能派上用场的地方寥寥无几。

sentences.en: Like holding an umbrella in one hand and a cell phone in the other at the same time.
sentences.zh: 比如一只手拿伞，另一只手同时拿手机。

sentences.en: Which now is not a problem because I live in the Bay Area and it never rains.
sentences.zh: 现在这不是个问题了，因为我住在湾区，这里从不下雨。

sentences.en: And it was great for operating a potato racer on Thanksgiving.
sentences.zh: 而且感恩节时用它来操作压薯器真是太棒了。

sentences.en: Other than that, her $70,000 bionic hand has been kind of a buSt.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，她这副价值7万美元的仿生手多少有点鸡肋。

sentences.en: So I made $70,000 Thanksgiving mashed potatoes.
sentences.zh: 所以我做出了价值7万美元的感恩节土豆泥。

sentences.en: Is it worth it?
sentences.zh: 这值得吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不值得。

sentences.en: Which brings up another issue with advanced prosthetics.
sentences.zh: 这就引出了先进假肢的另一个问题。

sentences.en: How absurdly expensive they are.
sentences.zh: 它们贵得离谱。

sentences.en: Britt was lucky enough to have really good insurance which paid for the bulk of the price.
sentences.zh: 布里特很幸运，她买了好得多的保险，报销了绝大部分费用。

sentences.en: But a complex myoelectric arm can cost anywhere from $20,000 to $100,000.
sentences.zh: 但一副复杂的肌电手臂造价可能在2万到10万美元之间。

sentences.en: And even if you have good insurance, it can be a battle to get insurance companies to pay
sentences.zh: 而且就算你有好保险，要想让保险公司为哪怕最基础的假肢买单也是一场硬仗

sentences.en: for even the most basic types of prosthetics, let alone the experimental high-tech kinds.
sentences.zh: 更不用说那些实验性质的高科技假肢了。

sentences.en: But despite the high financial costs and all the functionality issues, Britt says a lot of
sentences.zh: 但尽管财务成本高昂，且存在种种功能问题，布里特说很多人

sentences.en: people still choose these types of advanced prosthetics over low-tech options in order to
sentences.zh: 为了迎合别人的期望，依然选择这类先进假肢，而不是低技术选项。

sentences.en: meet other people's expectations.
sentences.zh: 迎合别人的期望。

sentences.en: It seems like there's a little bit of an overbearing expectation that, like, if you're
sentences.zh: 似乎有一种过分沉重的期待，好像如果你

sentences.en: missing a limb, then you need to have a cyborg arm.
sentences.zh: 身体残缺，就必须得有一条赛博格手臂。

sentences.en: You need to be bionic.
sentences.zh: 你得是仿生人。

sentences.en: Because that's cool.
sentences.zh: 因为那很酷。

sentences.en: It gets you cool attention.
sentences.zh: 能为你赢得酷炫的关注。

sentences.en: Futuristic prosthetic technologies are exciting and draw a specific type of positive attention.
sentences.zh: 未来主义的假肢技术令人兴奋，并能吸引一种特定类型的正面关注。

sentences.en: And for a lot of people with limb differences, this attention can seem better than the alternative.
sentences.zh: 对于许多有肢体差异的人来说，这种关注似乎比别无选择要好。

sentences.en: When we wear a prosthesis in public, we attract attention.
sentences.zh: 当我们在公众场合佩戴假肢时，我们会吸引注意力。

sentences.en: But we're going to attract attention no matter what.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何我们都会吸引注意力的。

sentences.en: So the person has to decide with what are they more comfortable.
sentences.zh: 所以当事人必须决定他们更能接受哪一种。

sentences.en: This is Debbie Latour.
sentences.zh: 这位是黛比·拉图尔。

sentences.en: She's an occupational therapist and does educational consulting for prosthetics design.
sentences.zh: 她是一名职业治疗师，并为假肢设计提供教育咨询。

sentences.en: Debbie also has a congenital limb difference and occasionally uses a powered hand.
sentences.zh: 黛比天生也有肢体差异，偶尔会使用电动手。

sentences.en: She actually really likes hers.
sentences.zh: 她其实非常喜欢自己的假肢。

sentences.en: It's invaluable for doing things like typing.
sentences.zh: 对于打字之类的事情，它简直无价。

sentences.en: And I'm a university professor.
sentences.zh: 而且我是一名大学教授。

sentences.en: You know, I do a lot of bimanual activities.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我要做很多需要双手配合的活动。

sentences.en: And not using her prosthetic arm can come with its own probleMs.
sentences.zh: 而不使用她的假肢手臂也会带来它自己的问题。

sentences.en: If you've ever tried to push a grocery cart with one arm, I would challenge you to do it and be prepared to knock down a display at the end of an aisle.
sentences.zh: 如果你试过用单臂推购物车，我敢请你试试看，并做好撞倒过道尽头货架的准备。

sentences.en: Debbie may have a different relationship with her prosthetic hand.
sentences.zh: 黛比对她的假肢手可能会有不同的看法。

sentences.en: But she does agree with Britt that the way that high-tech limbs are viewed by people who don't have limb differences can be damaging.
sentences.zh: 但她和布里特一样认为，没有肢体差异的人看待高科技假肢的方式可能会带来伤害。

sentences.en: And a lot of that has to do with how we talk about them.
sentences.zh: 这在很大程度上与我们如何谈论它们有关。

sentences.en: Oftentimes, prosthetic technology is viewed as like the savior or the superhero type of thing that's going to give us all of these bionics.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，假肢技术被视为救世主或超级英雄似的东西，它将赋予我们所有的仿生能力。

sentences.en: Because it's a bionic arm, it's going to give us superhuman capacities.
sentences.zh: 因为它是一条仿生手臂，它就会赋予我们超人的能力。

sentences.en: But it's a process.
sentences.zh: 但这需要一个过程。

sentences.en: If you spend too much time on Twitter, like me, or you watch a lot of local news, then you've probably come across a very specific type of viral video about advanced prosthetics.
sentences.zh: 如果你像我一样在推特上花太多时间，或者看了很多地方新闻，那你大概遇到过一种非常特定的关于先进假肢的病毒式传播视频。

sentences.en: They're feel-good videos that feature a child with a limb difference being given a bionic arm with some sort of click-baity title.
sentences.zh: 它们是那种带有某种标题党风格的、让人感觉良好的视频，主角是一个获得了仿生手臂的肢体差异儿童。

sentences.en: Like, baby receives prosthetic arm, look at their reaction.
sentences.zh: 比如，宝宝装上假肢，看他们的反应。

sentences.en: Or 10-year-old opens up 3D-printed arm for the first time, see how they squeal.
sentences.zh: 或者10岁儿童首次打开3D打印手臂，看他们如何尖叫。

sentences.en: In 2012, a disability rights activist named Stella Young coined a phrase for exactly this type of video, inspiration porn.
sentences.zh: 2012年，一位名叫斯特拉·扬的残疾人权利活动家创造了一个词，专门用来形容这种类型的视频：激励色情。

sentences.en: She specifically used the word porn because she sees it as the objectification of one group for the benefit of another.
sentences.zh: 她特别使用了“色情”这个词，是因为在她看来，这是为了迎合一方而将另一方工具化、异化。

sentences.en: The media has always been about prosthetics being, like, savior technologies and, like, feel-good fluff pieces.
sentences.zh: 媒体一直以来都在宣传假肢是救世主般的技术，以及那种让人感觉良好的温情小品。

sentences.en: Look at this disabled kid or look at this disabled adult.
sentences.zh: 看看这个残疾儿童，或者看看这个残疾成年人。

sentences.en: And now their life is better because of this tech.
sentences.zh: 现在因为有了这项技术，他们的生活变好了。

sentences.en: You see this a lot in reaction videos of babies hearing for the first time after receiving a cochlear implant, too.
sentences.zh: 你在婴儿植入耳蜗后第一次听到声音的反应视频中也经常看到这一点。

sentences.en: These stories give people an unrealistic expectation of what advanced prosthetic devices can actually do for users.
sentences.zh: 这些故事给人们带来了不切实际的期望，让他们以为先进的假肢设备到底能为使用者做些什么。

sentences.en: And they show a very narrow version of what thriving looks like for people with a disability.
sentences.zh: 而且它们展示了残疾人繁荣发展的一种非常狭隘的愿景。

sentences.en: All those inspiration stories, all of those pity stories, all of those technology rescue stories,
sentences.zh: 所有那些励志的故事，所有那些博取同情的 ngunit 故事，所有那些技术拯救的故事，

sentences.en: all of those are a way, I think, for us to just cognitively contain difference.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，所有这些都是我们用来在认知上容纳差异的一种方式。

sentences.en: And we can't imagine that difference actually might be a form of flourishing.
sentences.zh: 而我们无法想象，差异其实也可能是一种绽放的形式。

sentences.en: This is Sarah Hendren.
sentences.zh: 这位是莎拉·亨德伦。

sentences.en: She teaches design and fine arts at Oling College of Engineering.
sentences.zh: 她在欧林工程学院教授设计和美术。

sentences.en: She's not a fan of these types of videos either.
sentences.zh: 她也不喜欢这类视频。

sentences.en: They teach us that the solution to someone having a limb difference is to build them a better hand.
sentences.zh: 它们教导我们，面对某人有肢体差异这一情况，解决方案就是为他们制造一只更好的手。

sentences.en: Or the solution to disability in general is to, quote, fix a body.
sentences.zh: 或者说广义上残疾的解决方案就是，引述一下，“修复身体”。

sentences.en: The next time we meet somebody who's blind, the next time we accompany our aging grandparent to the theater,
sentences.zh: 下次我们遇到失明的人，下次我们陪着年迈的祖父母去剧院，

sentences.en: the next time, you know, we encounter a person with Down syndrome on the street,
sentences.zh: 下次，你知道的，我们在街上遇到唐氏综合征患者，

sentences.en: we can only think of, oh, where's the cyborg rescue for this person?
sentences.zh: 我们脑子里只会想，哦，这个人的赛博格拯救在哪里？

sentences.en: You know, like, where is the kind of soft piano music swelling in the background?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就像，那种背景音乐里渐渐响起柔和钢琴曲的感觉。

sentences.en: You know, that kind of narrative.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，那种叙事。

sentences.en: And that is a flattened way of seeing the world.
sentences.zh: 那是一种扁平化的世界观。

sentences.en: It's not hard for people interested in building assistive tech to get caught up in this narrative, too.
sentences.zh: 对制造辅助技术感兴趣的人来说，也很容易陷入这种叙事中。

sentences.en: Hendren teaches a lot of engineering students,
sentences.zh: 亨德伦教过很多工程专业的学生，

sentences.en: and she worries that this type of narrow representation can enforce the idea that high-tech solutions are the only ones that matter.
sentences.zh: 她担心这种狭隘的代表性会强化这样一种观念：即高科技解决方案才是唯一重要的。

sentences.en: I say this with love.
sentences.zh: 我是带着爱意说这番话的。

sentences.en: It is a kind of slam dunk for, like, a young person who was interested in robotics,
sentences.zh: 对一个对机器人感兴趣、立志在世界上大展宏图的年轻人来说，

sentences.en: who broadly wants to do good in the world.
sentences.zh: 这简直是一次完美的扣篮得分。

sentences.en: High-tech prosthetic limbs looks like, you know, the center of that Venn diagram.
sentences.zh: 高科技假肢看起来就像是那个维恩图的正中心。

sentences.en: But it can obscure, then, what assistive technology could really be.
sentences.zh: 但它可能会掩盖辅助技术真正可以成为的样子。

sentences.en: It feels like the temptation for designers is to try to create an amazing new technology
sentences.zh: 设计师受到的诱惑似乎总是去尝试创造一项能够抹去一个人残疾的新技术，

sentences.en: that can erase a person's disability,
sentences.zh: 抹去一个人的残疾，

sentences.en: when maybe the better challenge is to try to design a world that can accommodate people with different types of bodies
sentences.zh: 而或许更好的挑战是去尝试设计一个能够包容具有不同身体类型

sentences.en: and different sets of abilities.
sentences.zh: 和不同能力水平的人的世界。

sentences.en: We've kind of chosen the messier way,
sentences.zh: 我们某种程度上选择了更棘手的一条路，

sentences.en: which is, like, trying to make every person who is not, quote-unquote, whole, whole again,
sentences.zh: 也就是试图让每一个不是，引述一下，“完整”的人重新变得完整，

sentences.en: when we could make kitchen counters or cars more accessible to begin with, that are more adaptable.
sentences.zh: 而本可以在一开始就让厨房台面或汽车更具可及性，使它们更具适应性。

sentences.en: In Britt's case, instead of selling her a $70,000 arm that makes it easier for her to use a potato ricer,
sentences.zh: 就布里特的例子而言，与其卖给她一副价值7万美元的手臂来让她更轻松地使用压薯器，

sentences.en: maybe we could design a potato ricer that's a little easier for someone with a different type of body to operate.
sentences.zh: 或许我们可以设计一款对身体类型不同的人来说稍微容易操作一点的压薯器。

sentences.en: A lot of people with limb differences can do tasks better with no prosthesis at all
sentences.zh: 许多有肢体差异的人完全不用假肢反而能把事情做得更好，

sentences.en: because they've developed their own adaptations.
sentences.zh: 因为他们已经发展出了自己的适应方式。

sentences.en: And for many others, the lower-tech options are actually a lot more functional.
sentences.zh: 对许多其他人来说，技术含量较低的选项实际上实用性要高得多。

sentences.en: There are things like split-hook prostheses, which are super reliable because they have no electronic components
sentences.zh: 有诸如分钩式假肢之类的东西，它们超级可靠，因为它们没有任何电子元件，

sentences.en: and don't attempt to resemble a hand at all.
sentences.zh: 并且根本不试图去模仿一只手。

sentences.en: There are over 2 million people in the United States living with a limb difference,
sentences.zh: 美国有超过200万生活在肢体差异中的人，

sentences.en: and every single one of those experiences is different.
sentences.zh: 而每一个这样的经历都是独一无二的。

sentences.en: Satisfaction with a prosthetic device can depend on which limb is affected or how many limbs are affected,
sentences.zh: 对假肢设备的满意度可能取决于受影响的是哪只肢体，或者受影响的肢体有多少，

sentences.en: and it can depend on how high or low an amputation might be, or whether or not you were born with it.
sentences.zh: 它还可能取决于截肢部位的高低，或者你是否天生如此。

sentences.en: There's no such thing as a one-size-fits-all solution to assistive tech,
sentences.zh: 辅助技术根本不存在什么“一刀切”的解决方案，

sentences.en: and we need to listen to what people actually need in order to navigate the world.
sentences.zh: 我们需要倾听人们在在这个世界中穿梭时真正需要什么。

sentences.en: I want to make space for, like, critiquing these things,
sentences.zh: 我想留出空间来批判这些东西，

sentences.en: because otherwise then we just have to be grateful all the time for, like, whatever gets invented.
sentences.zh: 因为否则的话，我们就只能对任何被发明出来的新玩意儿时刻感恩戴德了。

sentences.en: These days, Britt doesn't use her high-tech bionic arm and doesn't even wear a cosmetic prosthesis anymore.
sentences.zh: 如今，布里特不再使用她那高科技的仿生手臂，甚至连装饰性假肢也不戴了。

sentences.en: But a couple of times a week, she uses an activity-specific device,
sentences.zh: 但一周有那么几次，她会使用一种针对特定活动的设备，

sentences.en: which is a type of prosthetic socket with swappable attachments for things like exercising.
sentences.zh: 这是一种带有可更换附件的假肢接受腔，用于锻炼等活动。

sentences.en: It doesn't try to resemble a natural hand at all, and is much simpler than her bionic hand.
sentences.zh: 它根本不试图模仿自然的手，而且比她的仿生手简单得多。

sentences.en: She has a clamp attachment, so she can do kettlebell swings,
sentences.zh: 她有一个夹具附件，所以她可以做壶铃摇摆，

sentences.en: and another called a mushroom that she uses to do balanced push-ups.
sentences.zh: 还有一个叫蘑菇头的附件，她用来做平衡俯卧撑。

sentences.en: It's called that because it looks like a mushroom.
sentences.zh: 它之所以叫这个名字，是因为它长得像个蘑菇。

sentences.en: And it's not like Britt is anti-technology.
sentences.zh: 而且并不是说布里特反技术。

sentences.en: Actually, she's surprisingly optimistic about it.
sentences.zh: 事实上，她对此出奇地乐观。

sentences.en: I do think that the technology will improve.
sentences.zh: 我的确认为技术会进步。

sentences.en: I do think that there will be better options.
sentences.zh: 我的确认为会有更好的选择。

sentences.en: And maybe in my lifetime, I'll get another arm that will help me do the potato ricing a little bit better.
sentences.zh: 也许在我有生之年，我会得到另一只手臂，能帮我把土豆泥压得更好一点。

sentences.en: But in the meantime, she's not going to just wait around for the perfect arm to get invented.
sentences.zh: 但在此期间，她不会只是原地等待完美的胳膊被发明出来。

sentences.en: She'll keep using her mushroom and her kettlebell clamp, and sometimes no prosthesis at all.
sentences.zh: 她会继续使用她的蘑菇头和壶铃夹具，有时甚至完全不用假肢。

sentences.en: And she'll continue using all the strategies she's developed to navigate a world that wasn't built for her.
sentences.zh: 她将继续使用她所开发的所有策略，来应对一个并非为她而建的世界。

sentences.en: This story was produced by Vivian Leigh and edited by Chris Berube and Emmett Fitzgerald.
sentences.zh: 这个故事由维维安·利制作，克里斯·伯鲁比和埃米特·菲茨杰拉德剪辑。

sentences.en: When we come back, we have a story about how the world is not actually designed for you.
sentences.zh: 当我们回来时，我们将讲述一个关于这个世界其实并非为你而设计的故事。

sentences.en: It was designed for the average person.
sentences.zh: 它是为普通人设计的。

sentences.en: Your world has not been designed for you.
sentences.zh: 你的世界并非为你而设计。

sentences.en: In large part, it has been designed for the average person.
sentences.zh: 在很大程度上，它是为普通人设计的。

sentences.en: Throughout your education, you've been given standardized tests and been graded by how well you perform compared to the average.
sentences.zh: 在你的整个受教育过程中，你一直在做标准化测试，并根据你与平均水平相比的表现来打分。

sentences.en: Building codes, insurance rates, the Dow Jones, all these measurements are based around the concept of an average.
sentences.zh: 建筑规范、保险费率、道琼斯指数，所有这些测量标准都是围绕平均值的概念建立的。

sentences.en: And it's okay.
sentences.zh: 这没关系。

sentences.en: We know you're not average.
sentences.zh: 我们知道你不是普通人。

sentences.en: You're really special.
sentences.zh: 你真的很特别。

sentences.en: Oh, thanks, Avery Truffleman.
sentences.zh: 哦，谢谢你，艾弗里·特拉夫曼。

sentences.en: Well, I mean it.
sentences.zh: 我是认真的。

sentences.en: You're not average.
sentences.zh: 你不是普通人。

sentences.en: No one is.
sentences.zh: 没有人是。

sentences.en: Not completely.
sentences.zh: 并非完全如此。

sentences.en: But the concept of average affects us all.
sentences.zh: 但平均值的概念影响着我们所有人。

sentences.en: Everything seemed to be based around this reference point of average.
sentences.zh: 一切似乎都建立在平均值这个参考点上。

sentences.en: And obviously, everything about society is built this way.
sentences.zh: 显然，社会的方方面面都是这样构建的。

sentences.en: But I'd never really thought of it until I dug into this new science that I'm a part of.
sentences.zh: 但在我深入研究我所参与的这门新科学之前，我从未真正思考过这一点。

sentences.en: This is Todd Rose.
sentences.zh: 这是托德·罗斯。

sentences.en: My name is Todd Rose.
sentences.zh: 我叫托德·罗斯。

sentences.en: I am the director of the Mind, Brain, and Education program at the Harvard Graduate School of Education.
sentences.zh: 我是哈佛大学教育研究生院“心智、大脑与教育”项目的主任。

sentences.en: He's also the author of the book, The End of Average.
sentences.zh: 他也是《平均的终结》一书的作者。

sentences.en: But to get to that, first, we have to start with the beginning of average.
sentences.zh: 但要理解这一点，首先，我们得从平均的起源说起。

sentences.en: Because it wasn't always a thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这并非自古就有的概念。

sentences.en: The concept of average, as we know it, was pioneered by a Belgian mathematician and astronomer named Adolphe Ketelet.
sentences.zh: 我们所知的平均概念，是由一位名叫阿道夫·凯特莱的比利时数学家和天文学家开创的。

sentences.en: So Ketelet is the person who actually coins the term the average man.
sentences.zh: 所以，凯特莱正是创造“平均人”这个术语的人。

sentences.en: And he is, in like the 1830s, he is actually an astronomer in Belgium.
sentences.zh: 大约在19世纪30年代，他在比利时担任天文学家。

sentences.en: Today, the way that most people get a handle on any set of numbers is to calculate the average.
sentences.zh: 今天，大多数人掌握任何一组数据的方法都是计算平均值。

sentences.en: But in Ketelet's time, astronomers were some of the only people who did this.
sentences.zh: 但在凯特莱的时代，天文学家是仅有的会这么做的人之一。

sentences.en: Basically, averages were a way to compensate for the imprecise tools that astronomers were working with in 1830.
sentences.zh: 基本上，平均值是用来弥补1830年代天文学家所使用的工具不够精确的问题。

sentences.en: If you were trying to time the movement of Saturn, you would etch little scratches on your glass of your telescope.
sentences.zh: 如果你试图测算土星的运行时间，你会在望远镜的镜片上刻下细小的划痕。

sentences.en: And as soon as it crossed one, you'd start counting.
sentences.zh: 一旦它穿过其中一条划痕，你就开始计时。

sentences.en: And you'd stop counting after it crossed the other.
sentences.zh: 当它穿过另一条划痕时，你便停止计时。

sentences.en: And then you'd write it down.
sentences.zh: 然后你把它记录下来。

sentences.en: But you can imagine, like even if you're off by half a second, it's going to introduce a lot of error.
sentences.zh: 但你可以想象，即使你偏差了半秒钟，也会产生大量的误差。

sentences.en: And so they realized if they wanted to make sense of taming the heavens, they needed more precision in their estimates.
sentences.zh: 因此他们意识到，如果他们想理解并驾驭浩瀚星空，他们的估算就需要更高的精确度。

sentences.en: And they realized that if you had, say, 10 measurements, and they were all slightly different,
sentences.zh: 他们意识到，如果你有，比方说10次测量结果，而且它们都略有不同，

sentences.en: if you added them together and divided them by 10, you'd get a better approximation of the true measurement.
sentences.zh: 如果你将它们相加并除以10，你就会得到对真实测量值更好的近似。

sentences.en: If you just average together our measurements, you're way more likely to be closer to the truth, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你把我们的测量结果平均起来，你离真相就会近得多，对吧？

sentences.en: And you end up getting kind of a bell curve of measurement errors.
sentences.zh: 最终你会得到一种呈钟形曲线的测量误差分布。

sentences.en: Ketelay was the first to take this tool of astronomers and apply it to people.
sentences.zh: 凯特莱是第一个将天文学家的这一工具应用到人类身上的人。

sentences.en: In the early 1840s, Ketelay finds a data set of the chest measurements of 5,738 Scottish soldiers.
sentences.zh: 在19世纪40年代初，凯特莱找到了一个包含5738名苏格兰士兵胸围的数据集。

sentences.en: Ketelay added together each of the measurements and divided it by the total sum of the soldiers.
sentences.zh: 凯特莱将每个测量值加起来，然后除以士兵的总数。

sentences.en: And that result, 39 and three quarters inches, was one of the very first times a scientist had calculated the average size of a human feature.
sentences.zh: 这个结果是39又四分之三英寸，这是科学家历史上首次计算出人类特征的平均尺寸。

sentences.en: But he brings with it the idea of truth, that the average chest size is true and that all the individuals are like error,
sentences.zh: 但他同时也带来了关于真理的概念，即平均胸围是真的，而所有个体都像是误差，

sentences.en: that nature is striving for the average soldier.
sentences.zh: 大自然正在努力塑造平均的士兵。

sentences.en: This means the average measurement is the true measurement, the platonic ideal.
sentences.zh: 这意味着平均测量值就是真实的测量值，即柏拉图式的理想状态。

sentences.en: Ketelay, the perfect Scottish soldier, has a chest that is 39 and three quarters inches, according to Ketelay.
sentences.zh: 按照凯特莱的说法，完美的苏格兰士兵凯特莱，其胸围是39又四分之三英寸。

sentences.en: So he's the one that decides not only is average mathematically useful, it's morally the way to think about people.
sentences.zh: 因此，正是他决定了平均值不仅在数学上有用，而且在道德上也是看待人们的方式。

sentences.en: And so he basically finds averages anywhere he can possibly find them.
sentences.zh: 于是他基本上在任何可能的地方寻找平均值。

sentences.en: And he just has like a field date.
sentences.zh: 他简直乐此不疲。

sentences.en: He measures all kinds of other people and averages them.
sentences.zh: 他测量了各种各样的人并算出他们的平均值。

sentences.en: He creates something called the Ketelay Index for measuring ratios of average height and average weight.
sentences.zh: 他创造了一种名为“凯特莱指数”的东西，用于衡量平均身高和平均体重的比例。

sentences.en: And actually, we still use it today.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们今天仍在使用它。

sentences.en: Just now it's called the Body Mass Index, or BMI.
sentences.zh: 只不过现在它被称为身体质量指数，即BMI。

sentences.en: Ketelay would say, if you talked about height, everyone, if they were optimally fed,
sentences.zh: 凯特莱会说，如果谈到身高，每个人，如果他们得到了充足的营养，

sentences.en: if they were under the same environmental conditions, would have been average.
sentences.zh: 如果他们在相同的环境条件下，都会是平均身高。

sentences.en: So his view was that what you're striving for is the continual improvement of the average of the group.
sentences.zh: 所以他的观点是，你所追求的是群体平均水平的不断提高。

sentences.en: And it wasn't all just physical.
sentences.zh: 而且这不单单局限于身体特征。

sentences.en: Ketelay combs through various data sets for marriages, murders, and suicides, and calculates the averages for them.
sentences.zh: 凯特莱翻阅了关于婚姻、谋杀和自杀的各种数据集，并计算了它们的平均值。

sentences.en: He figures out there's such a thing as a normal suicide rate, which is really, really bizarre at the time.
sentences.zh: 他发现存在着所谓的正常自杀率，这在当时听起来非常非常离奇。

sentences.en: Almost scandalous.
sentences.zh: 简直可以说是骇人听闻。

sentences.en: Nowadays, when we're so used to the stability of big, massive amounts of data, that it's hard to put yourself in their shoes.
sentences.zh: 如今，我们对海量大数据的稳定性习以为常，很难设身处地去理解他们当时的感受。

sentences.en: But like, back then, they really thought that something like, say, suicide was such a personal decision that there couldn't possibly be any pattern there.
sentences.zh: 但在那时，人们真的认为诸如自杀之类的事件是极其个人的决定，不可能存在任何规律。

sentences.en: But suddenly there were patterns of body size, of intelligence, of birth, of death.
sentences.zh: 但突然之间，体型、智力、出生和死亡都出现了规律。

sentences.en: People became statistics.
sentences.zh: 人们变成了统计数字。

sentences.en: Their behavior starts to become predictable.
sentences.zh: 他们的行为开始变得可预测。

sentences.en: Suddenly, human life went by the numbers.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，人类的生活由数字来掌控。

sentences.en: So obviously, the first interpretation is, well, wait a minute, maybe there's no free will, right?
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，第一种解读就是，等一下，也许根本没有自由意志，对吧？

sentences.en: Maybe there's laws of society just like there's laws of physics.
sentences.zh: 也许社会规律就像物理规律一样存在。

sentences.en: And so that kick-started a whole bunch of people like, you know, like Karl Marx, who loved Ketelay.
sentences.zh: 这引发了许多人的共鸣，你知道的，比如卡尔·马克思，他就很崇拜凯特莱。

sentences.en: And Ketelay becomes a huge star.
sentences.zh: 凯特莱成了一颗耀眼巨星。

sentences.en: In his time, Ketelay was up there with the likes of Sir Isaac Newton.
sentences.zh: 在那个时代，凯特莱的地位堪与艾萨克·牛顿爵士比肩。

sentences.en: His science of averages was this remarkable, cutting-edge way to assess the health, wellness, and progress of populations.
sentences.zh: 他的平均值科学是一种卓越的、前沿的方法，用来评估人口的健康、福祉和发展。

sentences.en: He's really active in the 1820s, 1830s, 1840s, all the way into like the 50s and 60s.
sentences.zh: 他在1820年代、1830年代、1840年代都非常活跃，一直持续到50年代和60年代。

sentences.en: And the 1860s brings us to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 1860年代迎来了美国南北战争，

sentences.en: Civil War, and to another superfan of Ketelay's science of averages, Abraham Lincoln.
sentences.zh: 也迎来了凯特莱平均值科学的另一位超级粉丝——亚伯拉罕·林肯。

sentences.en: When the Civil War is going in the North, Lincoln actually decides, I mean, they're kind of getting their butt kicked, frankly.
sentences.zh: 当北方爆发内战时，林肯实际上决定……坦白说，他们当时被打得有点落花流水。

sentences.en: In large part because this war had gotten so huge and unwieldy, Lincoln doesn't really have a handle on the Northern Army.
sentences.zh: 很大程度上是因为这场战争变得如此庞大而难以驾驭，林肯对北方军队根本无法掌控。

sentences.en: And he's like, look, we don't even know who our soldiers are.
sentences.zh: 他当时想，瞧，我们甚至不知道我们的士兵都是些什么人。

sentences.en: We don't know how well-fed they are.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道他们是否吃得饱。

sentences.en: We don't know what kind of armor they need.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道他们需要什么样的盔甲。

sentences.en: We don't know anything about them.
sentences.zh: 我们对他们一无所知。

sentences.en: Lincoln decided that the Union Army needed more information about its soldiers in order to best distribute resources.
sentences.zh: 林肯决定，为了最好地分配资源，联邦军队需要更多关于士兵的信息。

sentences.en: So he ordered this enormous study to assess the Union Army physically, medically, and mentally.
sentences.zh: 于是他下令进行一项庞大的研究，从身体、医疗和心理方面评估联邦军队。

sentences.en: And then, in explicit obedience to Ketelay's new science, averages were calculated and reported.
sentences.zh: 然后，严格遵照凯特莱的新科学，计算并报告了各种平均值。

sentences.en: They actually say, basically, we're following the father of this new field, Ketelay.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上是说，基本上，我们正在追随这个新领域的奠基人凯特莱。

sentences.en: These freshly calculated averages informed the distributions of food rations and the design of weapons.
sentences.zh: 这些新计算出的平均值指导了口粮的分发和武器的设计。

sentences.en: For example, if you were going to create muskets, well, how far is the trigger?
sentences.zh: 例如，如果你要制造滑膛枪，那么扳机应该设在多远？

sentences.en: And you could actually calculate average reach for a soldier.
sentences.zh: 你实际上可以计算出士兵的平均手臂够到的距离。

sentences.en: This also affected military uniforms, which used to be all custom-sown.
sentences.zh: 这也影响了军服，过去军服都是全部定制缝制的。

sentences.en: But in the Civil War, so many people had to be outfitted that custom uniforms would be impossibly expensive.
sentences.zh: 但在内战中，有太多的人需要配备服装，定制军服的成本将会高得不可思议。

sentences.en: So the uniforms had to be mass-produced.
sentences.zh: 所以军服必须大规模生产。

sentences.en: But they couldn't be just all one big floppy size.
sentences.zh: 但它们不能全都是同一个宽松的大号。

sentences.en: And so now they're realizing, oh, well, you know, if we break it into subtypes, like there's a large, and this is what we mean by it.
sentences.zh: 于是现在他们意识到，哦，好吧，你知道的，如果我们把它分成不同的子类型，比如有大号，这就是我们的标准。

sentences.en: You know, this big of a torso, this broad of shoulders, you know, small, medium, large.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，多大的躯干，多宽的肩膀，你知道的，小号、中号、大号。

sentences.en: That's going to carry over into the way they think about the mass production of clothing.
sentences.zh: 这将延续到他们对服装大规模生产的思考方式中。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The sizes small, medium, and large, which might be on your t-shirt tag.
sentences.zh: 可能印在你T恤标签上的小号、中号和大号尺码。

sentences.en: Those came out of this massive Civil War study.
sentences.zh: 它们就源于内战时期的这项大规模研究。

sentences.en: So you can thank Ketelay and Lincoln for that.
sentences.zh: 所以你得为此感谢凯特莱和林肯。

sentences.en: This study in the Civil War was the basis for the American military's long-standing philosophy of standardized, average-based design.
sentences.zh: 内战中的这项研究构成了美军长期以来坚持的标准化、基于平均值的设计哲学的基石。

sentences.en: And that's going to become the fundamental design philosophy from the Civil War forward.
sentences.zh: 这将成为从南北战争以后基本的军事设计哲学。

sentences.en: So in 1926, when the Army was designing its first-ever fighter plane cockpit,
sentences.zh: 所以在1926年，当军队设计其历史上第一架战斗机座舱时，

sentences.en: engineers measured the physical dimensions of hundreds of male pilots and used this data to standardize cockpit dimensions.
sentences.zh: 工程师们测量了数百名男性飞行员的身体尺寸，并利用这些数据来标准化座舱的尺寸。

sentences.en: Of course, the possibility of female pilots was never considered.
sentences.zh: 当然，压根没有考虑过会有女飞行员的可能性。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 理所当然。

sentences.en: The size and shape of the seat, the distance to the pedals and the stick, the height of the windshield,
sentences.zh: 座椅的大小和形状、到踏板和操纵杆的距离、风挡的高度，

sentences.en: even the shape of the flight helmets were all made to conform to the average 1920s male pilot, which changed the way the pilots were selected.
sentences.zh: 甚至飞行头盔的形状，全都是为了迎合20世纪20年代的平均男性飞行员而制造的，这改变了飞行员的选拔方式。

sentences.en: You basically then select people that fit into that and then exclude people that don't.
sentences.zh: 基本上，你挑选符合这些尺寸的人，然后把不符合的人排除在外。

sentences.en: And this cockpit design worked okay, up to World War II.
sentences.zh: 这种座舱设计运行得还算可以，一直到二战时期。

sentences.en: What happened was, though, is that in World War II, it became an Air Force war, right?
sentences.zh: 然而发生的情况是，在二战中，这变成了一场空军的战争，对吧？

sentences.en: That was the first time when the Air Force would be the determinant of who was going to win the war.
sentences.zh: 那是空军首次成为决定谁将赢得战争的关键。

sentences.en: And we absolutely ran out of pilots.
sentences.zh: 而我们的飞行员绝对不够用了。

sentences.en: The government recruited hundreds of new pilots and expanded military aviation.
sentences.zh: 政府招募了数百名新飞行员，并扩大了军事航空规模。

sentences.en: They spent a bunch of money on fancy new planes, although the cockpits were still designed for the average 1920s male pilot.
sentences.zh: 他们在豪华的新飞机上花了一大笔钱，尽管座舱仍然是为20世纪20年代的平均男性飞行员设计的。

sentences.en: And this new big, bad military force was going to fly the fastest and the highest and be the beSt.
sentences.zh: 这支全新的、气势汹汹的强大军事力量将要飞得最快、最高，成为最优秀的队伍。

sentences.en: But that's not what happened.
sentences.zh: 但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: They actually had a pretty massive decline in performance, including just a rash of deaths.
sentences.zh: 他们的表现实际上出现了相当大规模的下滑，包括发生了一连串的坠机死亡事故。

sentences.en: Pilots were dying all the time.
sentences.zh: 飞行员们一直在牺牲。

sentences.en: Even after the war ended, just in training, they could not control their planes.
sentences.zh: 甚至在战争结束后，仅仅在训练中，他们也无法控制自己的飞机。

sentences.en: It became kind of part of the culture of the Air Force where, hey, it's just really dangerous to fly.
sentences.zh: 这成了空军文化的一部分，那就是，嘿，飞行本来就真的很危险。

sentences.en: No one knew what was going on.
sentences.zh: 没有人知道发生了什么。

sentences.en: Some people thought, well, these ain't propeller planes anymore.
sentences.zh: 有些人认为，这些不再是螺旋桨飞机了。

sentences.en: Maybe these new pilots just can't deal with the new aviation technology.
sentences.zh: 也许这些新飞行员只是应付不了新的航空技术。

sentences.en: And then they were like, well, maybe you got to train them better.
sentences.zh: 然后他们觉得，也许你们得更好地训练他们。

sentences.en: And they did their better training prograMs.
sentences.zh: 于是他们实施了更好的训练计划。

sentences.en: And that didn't work.
sentences.zh: 但那不管用。

sentences.en: After blaming the pilots, the training programs, and the technology, it finally dawns on them, what if it's the cockpit?
sentences.zh: 在责备了飞行员、训练计划和技术之后，他们终于恍然大悟：会不会是座舱的问题？

sentences.en: Maybe it doesn't fit us anymore.
sentences.zh: 也许它不再适合我们了。

sentences.en: Their first instinct is to think, we've just gotten bigger as a people, so the old average from 1922 is just too small, right?
sentences.zh: 他们的第一直觉是，我们这一代人变壮了，所以1922年的旧平均值太小了，对吧？

sentences.en: We're just bigger and badder, and like, let's build a better average.
sentences.zh: 我们变得更高大、更强壮了，让我们打造一个更好的平均值吧。

sentences.en: So in 1950, researchers at Wright Air Force Base in Ohio were tasked with finding this new average.
sentences.zh: 于是在1950年，俄亥俄州莱特空军基地的研究人员被委任寻找这个新的平均值。

sentences.en: And one of those researchers was a man named Gilbert S.
sentences.zh: 其中一位研究人员是一个名叫吉尔伯特·S·

sentences.en: Daniels.
sentences.zh: 丹尼尔斯的人。

sentences.en: Daniels was a Harvard graduate who had written his thesis on the average sizes of his classmates' hands.
sentences.zh: 丹尼尔斯是哈佛大学毕业生，他的毕业论文写的是同学们手掌的平均尺寸。

sentences.en: He was 23 years old.
sentences.zh: 他当时23岁。

sentences.en: Small, skinny, nerdy.
sentences.zh: 身材矮小、消瘦、带着书卷气。

sentences.en: Not a military man at all.
sentences.zh: 一点也不像个军人。

sentences.en: And he travels all over the country to different Air Force bases.
sentences.zh: 他走遍了全国各地的不同空军基地。

sentences.en: And his job is to take these tape measures and just measure like 147 different dimensions of body size.
sentences.zh: 他的工作就是拿着卷尺，测量体型的147个不同维度。

sentences.en: It's got to be the most tedious job ever.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是有史以来最枯燥乏味的工作。

sentences.en: And as Daniels is traveling around from base to base measuring thousands of airmen, he's realizing this incredible variability from person to person,
sentences.zh: 当丹尼尔斯从一个基地奔赴另一个基地，测量了数千名飞行员时，他意识到了人与人之间惊人的差异，

sentences.en: even within this limited demographic of young men.
sentences.zh: 即使在年轻男性这个有限的人口统计学群体内也是如此。

sentences.en: As he was measuring hands and legs and waists and foreheads, Daniels kept asking himself, how many pilots were actually average?
sentences.zh: 当他测量手部、腿部、腰部和前额时，丹尼尔斯不断地问自己：到底有多少飞行员真正处于平均水平？

sentences.en: So he reports back.
sentences.zh: 于是他回去汇报了。

sentences.en: So he goes to them and says, look, I think there's a problem with the average.
sentences.zh: 他去找他们并说道，听着，我认为平均值出了问题。

sentences.en: And he says, I just want to do this side study.
sentences.zh: 他说，我只想做这项辅助研究。

sentences.en: I want to know if we take the 10 dimensions of size that matter most for design.
sentences.zh: 我想知道，如果我们选取对设计最重要的10个尺寸维度，

sentences.en: Like, say, shoulder width, height, chest circumference, sleeve length, etc.
sentences.zh: 比方说，肩宽、身高、胸围、袖长等。

sentences.en: How many of these pilots are actually average on all 10 of those dimensions?
sentences.zh: 到底有多少飞行员在这全部10个维度上都处于平均水平？

sentences.en: Daniels crunched the numbers.
sentences.zh: 丹尼尔斯计算了这些数字。

sentences.en: And of the 4,063 pilots he measured, not a single airman was close to average in all of the 10 dimensions.
sentences.zh: 在他测量的4063名飞行员中，没有一名飞行员在所有10个维度上都接近平均水平。

sentences.en: None.
sentences.zh: 没有一个。

sentences.en: Not one.
sentences.zh: 一个也没有。

sentences.en: And it got even worse.
sentences.zh: 情况甚至更糟。

sentences.en: Like, if you just used three dimensions of size, less than 5% of the pilots were average on those.
sentences.zh: 如果你只使用三个体型维度，只有不到5%的飞行员在这三个维度上是平均水平。

sentences.en: So he quickly realizes, like, wait, now you know the problem.
sentences.zh: 所以他很快意识到，等等，现在你知道问题所在了。

sentences.en: If you are designing something for an average pilot, it's literally designed to fit nobody.
sentences.zh: 如果你为平均飞行员设计某样东西，它实际上就是设计得谁也不适合。

sentences.en: And in this new era of jet-powered aviation, where pilots were making split-second decisions that could be life or death,
sentences.zh: 在这个喷气式航空的新时代，飞行员们必须做出可能生死攸关的瞬间决断，

sentences.en: it really mattered that pilots could reach what they needed to reach in a cockpit.
sentences.zh: 飞行员能否在座舱里够到他们需要够到的东西，这真的至关重要。

sentences.en: The military sprang into action pretty much right away.
sentences.zh: 军方几乎立刻采取了行动。

sentences.en: For the military to be willing to basically drop generations of design philosophy, right?
sentences.zh: 军方居然愿意彻底抛弃几代人的设计哲学，这多不容易？

sentences.en: Because it doesn't take them more than a few years to just be like, you can't design on average anymore.
sentences.zh: 因为他们只花了几年时间就决定：不能再按平均值进行设计了。

sentences.en: Air Force engineers and contractors designed adjustable foot pedals and adjustable helmet straps and flight suits and adjustable seats.
sentences.zh: 空军工程师和承包商设计了可调节的脚踏板、可调节的头盔带、飞行服和可调节座椅。

sentences.en: You just can't believe that we were building planes with no adjustable seats.
sentences.zh: 你简直无法相信，我们过去制造飞机时居然没有可调节座椅。

sentences.en: That's how much faith we had in the average person.
sentences.zh: 我们对普通人的信任就是这样的。

sentences.en: Once all the adjustable elements and other design solutions were put into place, pilot performance soared.
sentences.zh: 一旦所有可调节的元素和其他设计方案落实到位，飞行员的表现就直线上升了。

sentences.en: And of course, now we take this for granted.
sentences.zh: 当然，现在我们把这视为理所当然。

sentences.en: That equipment should fit a wide range of body sizes instead of standardized around one average.
sentences.zh: 设备应该适应广泛的身体尺寸，而不是围绕一个平均值进行标准化。

sentences.en: You wouldn't buy a car that didn't have adjustable seats, right?
sentences.zh: 你不会买一辆没有可调节座椅的车，对吧？

sentences.en: That's just crazy.
sentences.zh: 那太疯狂了。

sentences.en: And it seeps into there pretty quickly in terms of automobiles.
sentences.zh: 在汽车方面，这种理念也很快渗透了进去。

sentences.en: And then you see what's interesting is the whole idea of ergonomics.
sentences.zh: 然后你会发现，有趣的是人体工学这个概念。

sentences.en: That all comes off of this period of time.
sentences.zh: 这都源于这一时期。

sentences.en: World War II jumpstarts the science of ergonomics, which is not just for office chairs.
sentences.zh: 二战催生了人体工学这门科学，它不仅仅适用于办公椅。

sentences.en: Well, it's really the study of work is what you could boil it down to.
sentences.zh: 嗯，归根结底，它实际上就是对工作的研究。

sentences.en: But it really is a matter of matching people's capacities to the job.
sentences.zh: 但它确实是一个将人的能力与工作相匹配的问题。

sentences.en: This is Professor Carissa Harris-Adamson, director of the UCSF-UC Berkeley Ergonomics Program.
sentences.zh: 这位是加州大学旧金山分校-加州大学伯克利分校人体工学项目主任卡里萨·哈里斯-亚当森教授。

sentences.en: It's really important not to go with the average a lot of the time.
sentences.zh: 很多时候，不依循平均值真的很重要。

sentences.en: If we want to incorporate, say, a handle into something, well, we'll look up the anthropometry data
sentences.zh: 如果我们想在某物中加入，比方说一个把手，我们会查阅人体测量数据，

sentences.en: and make sure we identify the grip span that we think is beSt.
sentences.zh: 并确保确定我们认为最佳的握距。

sentences.en: Or if we're designing a crank and we want it to be at a certain height,
sentences.zh: 或者如果我们正在设计一个摇柄，并希望它处于某个高度，

sentences.en: then we will go back to the anthropometry data and figure out what makes the most sense
sentences.zh: 我们就会重新查看人体测量数据，找出最合理的方案，

sentences.en: to accommodate as much of the population as we can.
sentences.zh: 以便尽可能适应更多的人群。

sentences.en: Keeping in mind that in the U.S., most of the measurements we base our designs on
sentences.zh: 请记住，在美国，我们设计所依据的大多数测量数据

sentences.en: still come from the U.S.
sentences.zh: 仍然来自美国

sentences.en: Army.
sentences.zh: 陆军。

sentences.en: That's primarily the source that we use in, say, ergonomic books or when we're designing for the workplace.
sentences.zh: 这主要是我们在诸如人体工学书籍或为工作场所设计时使用的来源。

sentences.en: And what we found is that those numbers are actually all pretty representative today,
sentences.zh: 我们发现，除了体重和腹围之外，

sentences.en: except for weight and abdominal girth.
sentences.zh: 这些数字在今天实际上都具有相当的代表性。

sentences.en: Which is part of why the world is so hard for heavier people to navigate.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么这个世界对较胖的人来说如此难以适应的部分原因。

sentences.en: The military might be considered a more fit population than the rest of us.
sentences.zh: 军队的人群可能被认为比我们其余的人更健康。

sentences.en: So does this mean that, like, military measurements affect the way our cars are designed?
sentences.zh: 那么这是否意味着，军方的测量数据会影响我们汽车的设计方式？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对会的。

sentences.en: The measurements of our military personnel over the years affect just about everything.
sentences.zh: 多年来，我们军事人员的测量数据几乎影响了所有事情。

sentences.en: Military measurements are the most public and accessible.
sentences.zh: 军队的测量数据是最公开、最容易获得的。

sentences.en: And they work okay.
sentences.zh: 而且它们的效果还算不错。

sentences.en: They're not perfect, sure, but they're getting more inclusive.
sentences.zh: 它们当然不是完美的，但它们正变得越来越具有包容性。

sentences.en: They've done a really good job in accommodating more of the population,
sentences.zh: 鉴于女性现在已经成为我们军事力量中充满活力的一部分，

sentences.en: given that women are now a very vibrant part of our military force.
sentences.zh: 他们在适应更多人群方面做得非常出色。

sentences.en: When the military opted to design for a greater range of people,
sentences.zh: 当军队选择为更大范围的人群进行设计时，

sentences.en: they designed for a greater range of opportunity.
sentences.zh: 他们也就为更广泛的机会进行了设计。

sentences.en: Take, for example, Kim Campbell.
sentences.zh: 以金·坎贝尔为例。

sentences.en: She was a fighter pilot, and she flew a A-10 Warthog, and it's worth Googling.
sentences.zh: 她是一名战斗机飞行员，驾驶过A-10“疣猪”攻击机，非常值得在谷歌上搜索一下。

sentences.en: It is, like, the baddest-looking plane you're ever going to see.
sentences.zh: 它简直是你见过最酷炫的飞机。

sentences.en: That's Todd Rose again, by the way, helping us tell the story of Captain Campbell.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，这位又是托德·罗斯，他帮我们讲述坎贝尔机长的故事。

sentences.en: In 2003, Campbell was sent on a mission to assist some Marines who were trying to take a bridge in Iraq.
sentences.zh: 2003年，坎贝尔被派往执行一项任务，协助一些试图攻占伊拉克一座桥梁的海军陆战队员。

sentences.en: They were under heavy fire.
sentences.zh: 他们遭到猛烈火力攻击。

sentences.en: But on her way back, her plane gets shot, and she loses all control.
sentences.zh: 但在她返回的途中，她的飞机中弹了，她失去了所有的控制。

sentences.en: She has the option to eject right there and save her life,
sentences.zh: 她当时可以选择直接跳伞逃生以保住性命，

sentences.en: but then the plane spirals into Baghdad and kills a bunch of innocent people.
sentences.zh: 但那样飞机就会螺旋坠入巴格达，并杀死一群无辜的人。

sentences.en: So she says, like, I'm not going to do that.
sentences.zh: 所以她说，我不打算那样做。

sentences.en: She stabilizes it, which I don't even know how you do.
sentences.zh: 她稳住了飞机，我甚至不知道你是怎么做到的。

sentences.en: And she flies back, and then she says, look, I think I can land this plane.
sentences.zh: 她飞了回来，然后她说，听着，我想我能把这架飞机降落。

sentences.en: And she lands the massive, damaged, uncontrollable plane.
sentences.zh: 于是她降落了这架巨大、受损且无法控制的飞机。

sentences.en: It's an incredible heroic feat.
sentences.zh: 这是一个令人难以置信的英勇壮举。

sentences.en: Really unprecedented.
sentences.zh: 实属空前。

sentences.en: So, of course, Kim Campbell gets awards and distinctions.
sentences.zh: 所以，理所当然地，金·坎贝尔获得了各种奖励和殊荣。

sentences.en: And she is someone who could have never been one of the best pilots in the world,
sentences.zh: 如果军队没有改变他们的设计理念，

sentences.en: had the military not changed their design philosophy.
sentences.zh: 她根本不可能成为世界上最优秀的飞行员之一。

sentences.en: She's the beneficiary of a cockpit that's flexibly designed.
sentences.zh: 她是一个采用灵活设计的座舱的受益者。

sentences.en: Because she's, like, 5'4", and rail-thin,
sentences.zh: 因为她身高只有5英尺4英寸，瘦得像根竹竿，

sentences.en: and doesn't look anything remotely close to an average-sized pilot.
sentences.zh: 看起来跟平均身材的飞行员一点也不沾边。

sentences.en: When Kim gets into a cockpit, she has to put the seat all the way up
sentences.zh: 当金坐进驾驶舱时，她必须把座椅调到最高，

sentences.en: and pull the pedals all the way out.
sentences.zh: 把踏板拉到最远。

sentences.en: But it fits.
sentences.zh: 但它很合身。

sentences.en: This idea of equal fit as the foundation for how we think about real opportunity in society
sentences.zh: 这种将“平等合身”作为我们思考社会中真正机会的基础的理念，

sentences.en: I think has serious consequences for the future of design.
sentences.zh: 我认为对设计的未来有着深远的影响。

sentences.en: And this concept, that fit makes opportunity,
sentences.zh: 而“合身创造机会”这个概念，

sentences.en: it's an important one for Todd.
sentences.zh: 对托德来说非常重要。

sentences.en: Because he believes that we can design environments and equipment
sentences.zh: 因为他相信我们可以设计环境、设备

sentences.en: and even entire systems to accommodate more and more people.
sentences.zh: 甚至是整个系统，以适应越来越多的人。

sentences.en: When we think about how we design environments,
sentences.zh: 当我们思考如何设计环境时，

sentences.en: you know, in a lot of fields,
sentences.zh: 你知道，在很多领域，

sentences.en: we've made some progress around accommodating wider ranges of people.
sentences.zh: 我们在适应更广泛人群方面已经取得了一些进展。

sentences.en: And things like education,
sentences.zh: 而在教育之类的事情上，

sentences.en: we still actually design for this mythical average person
sentences.zh: 我们实际上仍然在为这个神话般的平均人进行设计，

sentences.en: under the assumption that if you design something that fit an average person,
sentences.zh: 其假设是如果你设计的东西适合平均人，

sentences.en: it would actually fit most people.
sentences.zh: 它实际上就会适合大多数人。

sentences.en: By re-examining the concept of the average and acknowledging its limitations,
sentences.zh: 通过重新审视平均值的概念并承认其局限性，

sentences.en: we can maybe start to consider other ways of assessing
sentences.zh: 我们或许可以开始考虑评估和分类的其他方式，

sentences.en: and categorizing test scores or clothing sizes or wellness or happiness or worth.
sentences.zh: 例如测试分数、服装尺码、健康、幸福感或价值。

sentences.en: We can pave the way for more people who are outside of the average.
sentences.zh: 我们可以为更多处于平均值之外的人铺平道路。

sentences.en: Because, really, no one is average.
sentences.zh: 因为说实话，没有人是平均的。
